source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Resting heart rate is generally lowest in infancy and rises gradually through childhood before reaching the adult range.","B":"Resting heart rate remains essentially unchanged from infancy through adulthood when the person is healthy and afebrile.","C":"Resting heart rate is generally higher in infants and young children and decreases toward the usual adult range with age.","D":"Resting heart rate is generally higher in healthy adults than in infants because cardiac output requirements increase with age."}}
source_row.rationale: Normal heart rate is generally higher in infants and young children compared to adults, gradually decreasing toward the typical adult range (about 60-100 beats/min) as the child grows older, reflecting normal age-related physiological changes in cardiovascular function.
source_row.source_detail: 2025 PALS Digital Reference Card, Vital Signs in Children table: age-specific normal heart-rate ranges from infancy through adolescence. Updated to 2025 AHA CPR/ECC science; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
